entry.title: Building a Hiring Plan That Survives Budget Cuts
entry.summary: Most hiring plans are built during optimistic periods, growth is projected, budget is approved, and a headcount plan gets laid out for the year. The plan rarely accounts for what happens when growth assumptions don't hold and a mid-year budget cut forces a rethink. Companies that handle this transition well share a few structural habits that companies caught flat-footed usually don't. The instinct during a budget cut is often to freeze the most expensive open roles first, since that produces the largest immediate savings. entry.title: Agentic orchestration: Enterprise AI organizations have a deployment problem, not a platform problem — and most are calling chatbots agents
entry.summary: Across 101 enterprises, agent orchestration is consolidating onto model-provider platforms — Anthropic’s Claude leads by a wide margin — chosen for the gravity of the underlying model and judged on reliable multi-step execution. But the ambition runs well ahead of the reality: most deployed “agents” are still chatbot wrappers, the control plane enterprises expect is deliberately hybrid to avoid lock-in, and real-time fiscal control over token burn remains the exception.
